title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting ('situation W', notes on deployment of stratified spaces, 1981-82). Σ is the disjoint union of the (deployed) strata. It carries a partial order x<y, read as 'y lies on the boundary piece of a higher stratum lying over x'. Write Σ*(n) for the space of chains x0<...<xn, i.e. the nerve of this topological poset, so Σ*(0)=Σ. The face maps named on the page are:
- s:(x<y)↦x (source) and b:(x<y)↦y (target), both Σ*(1)→Σ;
- s':(x<y<z)↦(x<z), b':(x<y<z)↦(y<z) and p:(x<y<z)↦(x<y), all Σ*(2)→Σ*(1).

The page collects these into the hexagonal diagram (40), made of two squares plus the two outer edges s to Σ.
- Top square: b∘s' = b∘b' (both give z). It is labelled cartesian, intended as Σ*(2) ≅ Σ*(1)×_{Σ,b,b}Σ*(1). The intended meaning is that the two boundary faces over z, coming from x and from y, meet exactly in the corner of chains x<y<z.
- Bottom square: b∘p = s∘b' (both give y). It is cartesian, Σ*(2) ≅ Σ*(1)×_{b,Σ,s}Σ*(1). This is the Segal / composable-pairs condition of a nerve.
- Left side: s∘s' = s∘p (both give x).

Claimed properties:
- The hooked arrows b, b', s' are proper 'bordant' immersions, i.e. inclusions of boundary faces.
- The plain arrows s, p are, in the equisingular case, proper fibrations. Better still, they are bundles of manifolds with boundary.
- For s:Σ*(1)→Σ, the fibrewise boundary is the image of s':Σ*(2)→Σ*(1). These are the pairs (x<z) admitting an intermediate y, i.e. z is not an immediate successor of x.
- For p, by the bottom cartesian square, the fibre over (x<y) is the s-fibre over y. Its boundary is the image of Σ*(3)→Σ*(2), (x<y<z<w)↦(x<y<w).
- Warning: s and p are not surjective. The image of s is the non-maximal x. The image of p is the (x<y) with y non-maximal.

The next page rewrites this index-wise: strata Σ_i, faces Σ_ij⊂Σ_j, fibrations s_ij:Σ_ij→Σ_i, corners Σ_ijk = Σ_ik∩Σ_jk, with the same hexagon (41).

Purpose: an axiomatics of 'deployment data' for a stratified space. This means compact manifolds with boundary or corners (the blown-up strata) together with proper fibrations of their boundary faces onto lower strata. From such data the original stratified space is to be recovered by collapsing along the fibrations, and the homotopy type is to be handled tamely.

In modern terms: the resolution/unfolding of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners carrying an iterated fibration structure, organized as a simplicial space (nerve of the stratification poset) with Segal-type cartesian squares.
errors: Top square 'cart' is not literally true pointwise. The set-theoretic fibre product Σ*(1)×_{b,b}Σ*(1) contains the diagonal pairs ((x<z),(x<z)), pairs with x,y incomparable, and pairs with y<x. It equals Σ*(2) only after restricting to x<y, or index-wise to i<j as on the next page (Σ_ijk = Σ_ik∩Σ_jk). It also needs the condition (next page, b)) that faces from incomparable indices are disjoint. So the square should read: Σ*(2) is the 'x<y' component of the fibre product, or the intersection of faces.
In the marginal note on p, the source should be Σ*(2) (p:Σ*(2)→Σ*(1)), not Σ*(1). The fibre boundary is the image of Σ*(3)→Σ*(2); the transcription garbles this.

The fibration claims are asserted only in the equisingular case and are not proved. The previous page itself notes that the 'equisingular non-singular' property is 'sans doute' a consequence of conditions 1° and 2°, which is unverified.

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified space by deployment data: blown-up strata (manifolds with boundary/corners) with boundary faces fibering properly over lower strata
ideas.modern_name: Resolution/unfolding of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with corners with iterated fibration structure; 'unzipping'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1960s–70); Verona (1984); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017, 'unzip')
ideas.where_published: Outlined in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology/stratified spaces and 'déploiement'; details unpublished

ideas.what: Organizing the deployment as the nerve Σ*(n) of a topological poset, with face maps s,b,s',b',p and a hexagon of two cartesian squares (Segal square plus corner-intersection square)
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial space / category object in spaces with Segal condition; exit-path category of a stratified space viewed as a topological poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1974) for the Segal condition; MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for exit paths

ideas.what: Fibrewise boundary of s given by image of the next face map s' (and of p by image of Σ*(3)), i.e. corners indexed by refinements of chains
ideas.modern_name: Boundary hypersurfaces/corners of a manifold with corners indexed by chains of strata (⟨k⟩-manifold structure)

ideas.what: Non-surjectivity remark: image of s = non-maximal points, image of p = chains whose top is non-maximal

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the deployment of a stratified space as a simplicial space (nerve of the order on Σ) whose face maps split into proper boundary embeddings and proper fibrations, subject to Segal-type cartesian squares. This anticipates treating the resolved stratified space as a 'category object' whose nerve satisfies Segal conditions. That viewpoint later appears in the exit-path / conically smooth stratified spaces literature (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), apparently without reference to this early formulation.
missed.quote: Les morphismes les plus importants dans la situation-W apparaissent dans le diagramme hexagonal suivant (40) ... où les flèches marquées ↪ ... sont des immersions bordantes (propres), et les flèches marquées → (en fait, s et p) sont (dans le cas équisingulier) fibrantes et propres
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historically early, explicit simplicial-space axiomatics for resolved stratified spaces, combining 'boundary inclusion' and 'fibration' face maps. It could be compared with AFT's unzipping and with recent work characterizing stratified spaces by their resolutions.

deep.surprise_reason: The deployment programme is announced in the Esquisse, and resolution of stratified spaces into manifolds with corners is now standard (Verona, ALMP, AFT). The specific nerve/hexagon formalism with Segal cartesian squares is a nice unpublished detail. However, it is mostly bookkeeping, and the top cartesian square is stated imprecisely.
transcription_corrections: Superscripts are Σ*(1), Σ*(2), Σ*(3) (asterisk), not Σ^α.

The diagram layout is a hexagon. Top row: Σ*(1) →b Σ. Middle: Σ (left), Σ*(2) →b' Σ*(1) (right). Bottom row: Σ*(1) →b Σ. The top-left Σ*(1) maps to Σ by s. Σ*(2) maps up to the top Σ*(1) by s' and down to the bottom Σ*(1) by p. The right Σ*(1) maps up to the top Σ by b and down to the bottom Σ by s. The bottom Σ*(1) maps to the left Σ by s. Both squares are labelled 'cart'.
Marginal insertion should read roughly: 'dans le cas de p: Σ*(2)→Σ*(1), la fibre des bords est l'image de Σ*(3)'.
The bracket under s:Σ*(1)→Σ reads approximately 'i.e. l'ens. des (x<y) tels que y ne soit pas successeur immédiat de x' (partly struck), describing the image of s'.
'ne sont pas même des surjectifs' — 'même' is struck and replaced by 'pas'; the final phrase reads 'celle de p est formée des (x<y) tels que y ne soit pas maximal'.
